candidates.summary: Backtested runway: replace the single 'cash / 3-month average net burn' number with an estimator that has been backtested on the company's own history (trailing-3 vs trailing-6 vs growth-trend vs known-obligations calendar). Show its measured past error as 'this runway number has been off by +/- N weeks on your data'.
candidates.hypothesis: The shipped runway (src/lib/finance/runway.ts: 3 complete months, flat net burn) and the Monte Carlo band (forecast.ts says it captures noise, not trends) are assumed good enough. On companies that are hiring, growing revenue, prepaying annual contracts or paying lumpy legal bills, a flat 3-month average misdates zero-cash by more than 1 month on a large share of months. A trend plus scheduled-obligations estimator cuts median absolute zero-cash-date error by at least 30% without being worse on steady companies. A runway figure with a stated, measured error builds more trust than Mercury Insights' free single number.
candidates.mve: Extend the seed generator with a profile parameter (steady, hiring ramp of +1 engineer every 2 months, revenue growth 0/5/15% per month, annual prepay months, a $40k legal one-off, a mid-history raise). Generate 200 companies over 36 months, each with a known true cash path. At every month t>=6, run each estimator on data up to t and compare its predicted zero-cash date to the realized one (simulate forward from the generator past asOf). Report median and P90 absolute error in weeks per profile, and P10-P90 band coverage for forecast.ts. Falsified if the 3-month average error stays under 4 weeks for at least 80% of company-months on all profiles, or if no alternative cuts error by at least 30% on the non-steady profiles.

candidates.summary: Runway levers ranked across all spend, not just SaaS waste: rank every lever by months of runway it recovers (delay hire N by 2 months, cap AI/cloud spend growth, move idle cash to treasury yield, renegotiate or pull forward an annual renewal, cut waste) and lead the product with that ranking rather than with 'Waste found'.
candidates.hypothesis: The product hero ('Finds the wasted spend... and turns it into months of runway') assumes SaaS waste is the biggest recoverable money for a seed startup. Payroll is commonly put at 60-80% of burn and software at 2-5%. So for the median synthetic seed company, waste recovery moves runway by under 0.5 months, while a single hire-timing or AI-spend-growth lever moves it by more than 1 month. A lever ranking would then be a stronger activation hook than the waste list.
candidates.mve: Parameterize the generator's spend mix by sampling payroll share (60-80%), software share (2-8%), AI/cloud growth (0-15% per month), headcount (3-30) and planted waste (0-3x today's). Across 500 companies, compute runway-months gained for each lever with the existing simulateSavings and scenario.ts planner: detected waste (from detectFindings), one hire delayed 2 months, AI spend growth capped at 3% per month, and a treasury yield of 4% on cash above 6 months of burn. Report the distribution of each lever's delta-months and the share of companies where waste is the top lever. Falsified if waste is the top lever in more than 50% of companies or if its median delta is at least 1 month.

candidates.summary: Detector robustness harness plus calibrated confidence: a shape-perturbation suite (shared company card instead of per-person cards, annual and quarterly billing, usage-priced SaaS, vendor rename or processor switch, billing-day drift, refunds, partial months, 3-40 person teams, mixed currencies). Each finding shows a confidence calibrated on the suite in place of the hard-coded CONFIDENCE constants, and is suppressed or downgraded to 'ask the owner' when its pattern is out of distribution.
candidates.hypothesis: The 100% precision and recall in docs/eval-results.md comes from 5 seeds of one company shape (Taco Robotics), with only descriptor noise varied. Nobody has checked that detectors tuned on that generator generalize. Under realistic shape changes at least one detector drops below 80% precision or recall. The zombie heuristic (idle cardholder for over 60 days) is the most fragile, because many small teams put every tool on one founder card, so 'bank data alone can tell which subscriptions are unused' fails. Calibrated confidence plus an ask-the-owner fallback would restore at least 90% precision for shown findings.
candidates.mve: Write scripts/stress-eval.ts. Take generateDemoCompany and apply composable perturbations: collapse all cardholders to 1-2 people, convert 30% of subscriptions to annual, shift billing days +/-5, rename descriptors (e.g. 'FIGMA' -> 'FIGMA INC DESIGN', SQ/TST/PAYPAL prefixes), inject refunds and duplicate pending-to-posted rows, scale to 5 or 40 cardholders, and add plausible negative controls (per-seat growth after hiring, two legitimately different design tools). Run the existing detectors across 50 seeds x each perturbation. Report precision and recall per detector per perturbation, and a reliability curve of hard-coded confidence vs observed precision. Falsified if every detector stays at or above 90% precision and recall under every perturbation.
evidence: docs/eval-results.md (5 seeds x 2 noise, one company shape)
README.md honest caveat: detectors developed against this generator; zombie is a heuristic

candidates.summary: Honest savings verification: harden 'verified savings' against false verification. Cases are an annual or quarterly tool with too little history to predict the next charge (savings.ts returns 'verified' immediately when nextExpected is null), a vendor that moved to another card or bank outside the feed, a downgrade that shows as a different descriptor, and a refund netted against a later charge. Report 'verified', 'likely', or 'unverifiable until <date>' with a measured false-verified rate.
candidates.hypothesis: The ROI and trust story (and any savings-based pricing) assumes absence of a charge in the Rho feed means the money was saved. Under realistic billing mixes, a material share (at least 15%) of 'verified' dollars are false, either verified before the next annual bill could have appeared or because the charge moved off-feed. A cadence-aware verifier with an explicit 'unverifiable' state cuts the false-verified dollar rate below 3% while delaying true verification by an acceptable median time.
candidates.mve: Simulate acted-on findings across 300 synthetic companies with a billing mix (70% monthly, 20% annual, 10% quarterly), ground-truth outcomes (truly cancelled 70%, silently still charging 15%, moved to an off-feed card 10%, downgraded under a new descriptor 5%) and history lengths of 1-24 months. Run the existing insights/savings.ts verifier and a cadence-aware variant (minimum observation window = max(known cadence, 13 months if only one charge seen), plus a descriptor-similarity search for successor charges). Report false-verified dollars, missed still-charging dollars and time-to-verify. Falsified if the current verifier's false-verified dollar rate is already under 5%.
evidence: sleep-research/IDEA_REPORT.md gap G1 (verification claimed as unique)

candidates.summary: Savings-decay pricing test plus materiality-gated digest: check two retention and monetization assumptions together. (a) Do verified savings keep pace with a subscription after the first cleanup? (b) Does a weekly Monday digest carry news most weeks? Ship pricing and cadence that follow the result, e.g. a one-time 'runway audit' fee plus a low monthly price for monitoring, and a digest that sends only when a materiality threshold is crossed (runway change of at least 2 weeks, a new finding of at least $X, a renewal decision) instead of every Monday.
candidates.hypothesis: 'Verified savings justify a subscription' and 'a weekly digest drives retention' are both untested. After the month-1 cleanup, new waste arrives slowly (a few new tools or price changes per year), so the median company's months 2-12 savings fall below a $99-299/mo price. Also, at least 60% of weekly digests would contain no item a founder needs to act on, which trains users to ignore them (notification-fatigue evidence). An audit-plus-monitor price and an event-gated digest would beat flat-subscription and every-Monday designs on value per message in simulation.
candidates.mve: Extend the generator with a 24-month arrival process for waste (new SaaS tools with Poisson rate 0.5-2/month, a 10% chance per year of a price rise per subscription, an employee departure every 6-12 months, a duplicate charge at 0.5%/month). Replay insights/digest.ts and the detectors weekly over 200 companies x 104 weeks. Measure (a) monthly newly found and verified $ after month 1 vs price points $49/$99/$299, and the share of companies where cumulative year-1 savings exceed the annual price, and (b) the share of weekly digests with at least one material item, alerts per week, and false spike-alerts on negative controls. Falsified if the median company's ongoing monthly verified savings exceed $299, or if at least 60% of weekly digests carry a material item.
evidence: research_notes/Runway product go to market/retention_features.md (digest ranked top retention feature; price anchors cfo.ai $295-375, Visible $59-149)
